key_insight: AutoGaze learns to 'look' only at informative video patches before the backbone model, autoregressively selecting a minimal set of multi-scale patches so downstream ViTs or MLLMs avoid processing redundant pixels while preserving prediction quality.
problem_solved: Scales multimodal video understanding to long, high-resolution videos by removing spatiotemporal redundancy and greatly reducing compute and memory cost of vision backbones and MLLMs.
method: Introduce a lightweight autoregressive module (AutoGaze) that selects a sparse, multi-scale subset of patches per step/frame and feeds only those to a ViT or MLLM.
Train end-to-end with next-token prediction augmented by reinforcement learning to balance task accuracy and selection sparsity (compute budget).
Plug-and-play design: sits before existing vision encoders or MLLMs, enabling compatibility with current multimodal architectures without changing core backbones.
impact: Enables efficient, scalable video understanding for longer and higher-resolution inputs—cutting compute and memory while retaining multimodal performance—so practitioners can deploy MLLMs on more realistic video workloads and budget-constrained environments.

paper_title: Attend Before Attention: Efficient and Scalable Video Understanding via Autoregressive Gazing
paper_authors: Baifeng Shi, Stephanie Fu, Long Lian, Hanrong Ye, David Eigen
